evidence.quote: We interpret such a behavior in the framework of an in-situ galaxy formation scenario, as a result of the transition from an early dust-obscured star-forming phase (mainly pinpointed by our FIR selection) to a late radio-loud quasar phase (preferentially sampled by the optical/radio selection).

claims.hypothesis: The FIR-to-radio luminosity ratio q_FIR evolves with redshift out to z ~ 4 in dusty star-forming galaxies.
claims.experiment: Cross-matched 80 H-ATLAS candidate lensed galaxies with FIRST (1.4 GHz), dedicated ATCA (2.1 GHz) follow-up, and literature JVLA data, using NIR and ALMA images for counterpart identification, and computed L_FIR, L_1.4GHz, and q_FIR for 28 detected sources (plus upper limits).
claims.result: Identified a weak decline of q_FIR with increasing z out to z <= 4, consistent with Magnelli et al. (2015) and Delhaize et al. (2017), with 3 sources at z >= 2 falling below q_FIR = 1.8.
claims.finding: There is a weak evolution of q_FIR with redshift out to z <= 4.

evidence.loc: The FIR-radio correlation for (candidate) lensed galaxies
evidence.quote: We find a weak yet appreciable decline of $q_{\rm FIR}$ with increasing $z$.

By taking advantage of the source brightness possibly enhanced by lensing magnification we identified a weak evolution with redshift out to $z\lesssim 4$ of the FIR-to-radio luminosity ratio $q_{\rm FIR}$, consistent with previous determinations at lower redshift based on different selections.

claims.hypothesis: FIR-selected lensed dusty star-forming galaxies and optically/radio-selected lensed quasars trace complementary evolutionary stages of an in-situ galaxy-BH co-evolution scenario in the q_FIR vs L_1.4GHz plane.
claims.experiment: Compared the q_FIR vs L_1.4GHz distribution of the 28 H-ATLAS sources with the lensed quasar sample of Stacey et al. (2018, 2019) and theoretical evolutionary tracks from Lapi et al. (2014, 2018).
claims.result: q_FIR decreases with increasing L_1.4GHz; ~90% of the FIR-selected sample lies above q_FIR = 1.8 (star-formation dominated), extending the trend of jet-dominated quasars to lower radio luminosities and matching the in-situ model track.
claims.finding: The decreasing trend of q_FIR with L_1.4GHz reflects a transition from an early dust-obscured star-forming phase to a late radio-loud quasar phase driven by the onset of jetted AGN emission.

evidence.loc: The FIR-radio correlation for (candidate) lensed galaxies
evidence.quote: Most relevantly, the majority of our sources lie ($\sim 90 \%$) in the region where radio emission is dominated by star formation, thus complementing the radio/optical selection adopted in (cite: Stacey2018) and actually extending to lower radio luminosities a consistent $q_{\rm FIR}$ vs. radio luminosity relation.

The agreement of the model prediction with the data is pleasingly good, and testifies that the behaviour of the FIR-radio correlation is physically driven by the onset of jetted radio emission, and consistent with a co-evolution scenario between star formation and BH growth.

why_this_data.value: FIR/submm selection with strong gravitational lensing magnification allows probing high-z dusty star-forming galaxies with minimal dust obscuration or foreground lens contamination, and high-resolution NIR/ALMA images enable reliable radio counterpart identification.

evidence.quote: In FIR/submm bands, high-z lensed dusty galaxies are particularly bright, while a negligible signal comes from the foreground lens, which is often a massive evolved elliptical at $z\lesssim 1$.

in order to establish whether a radio source is correctly assigned as a counterpart of our selected Herschel sample, we selected radio detections with at least $> 3\sigma_{\rm image}$ confidence level and then consider their position with respect to the optical/IR and the mm high angular resolution imaging.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Excluded H-ATLASJ090311.6+003907 (SDP.81) a priori because its radio emission likely originates from the AGN hosted by the foreground lens rather than the background lensed galaxy

evidence.quote: However, its radio emission is likely to be originated from the AGN hosted by the foreground lens ((cite: Tamura2015a), (cite: Rybak2020)); for this reason it has been excluded a priori as a possible counterpart.

limitations_admitted.value: Angular resolution of ATCA and FIRST radio observations (~5-10 arcsec) is insufficient to resolve lensed arcs

evidence.quote: The detected sources display a variety of radio morphologies: some of them show a compact radio emission, others instead feature a more extended structure or even multiple components, but the angular resolution of the observations is not enough to resolve any of the arcs possibly associated to lensing effects.

limitations_admitted.value: Selecting only the radio component nearest to the SPIRE peak may underestimate radio luminosity for multi-component radio sources

evidence.quote: We consider as a counterpart only the component nearest to the SPIRE peak position, whose radio detected emission overlaps with sources detected the in NIR or mm, even though this can result in a underestimation of the radio luminosity in case of multiple component radio sources.

limitations_admitted.value: Known positional offset between ALMA and HST/WFC3 counterparts is not corrected in the cutout maps

evidence.quote: Please note that the HST/WFC3 maps reported here do not take into account the well known positional offset between ALMA and HST counterparts ((cite: Dunlop2016), (cite: Rujopakarn2016)).

limitations_admitted.value: For unconfirmed lensing candidates lacking lens models or high-resolution radio data, the fraction of radio and SPIRE emission associated with the lensed object or multiple ALMA sources in the Herschel beam cannot be confirmed, and luminosities are not corrected for differential magnification

evidence.quote: for the remaining unconfirmed ones in absence of an accurate lens modelling and/or higher angular resolution observations, it is not possible to confirm whether or in which fraction the radio emission is associated to the lensed object.

Indeed, as showed in Figures 1 and 2, multiple sources entering the Herschel beam are detected in the ALMA (sub-)mm maps, leading to a possible overestimation of the effective FIR luminosity of the actual counterpart.

referee_caveats_inferred: Differential lensing magnification between compact radio (especially AGN core/jet) and extended FIR dust emission could artificially alter both q_FIR and apparent L_1.4GHz since uncorrected luminosities are used in the L_1.4GHz vs q_FIR plot.

Assuming a single constant radio spectral index alpha = -0.7 across all sources (including potential flat-spectrum or steep-spectrum AGN) introduces systematic uncertainty in K-corrections and 2.1-to-1.4 GHz conversions.
